Definition: a primary verb; to break (specially, of bread):--break.
KeyPassages: Matthew 14:19; Matthew 15:36; Mark 8:6; Luke 22:19; Acts 2:46; 1 Corinthians 10:16
BiblicalUsage: Klao means to break, specially of bread. Matthew 14:19 and Matthew 15:36 and Mark 8:6 have Jesus taking the loaves, blessing, and breaking them for the multitudes, Luke 22:19 has Him taking bread at the supper, giving thanks, and breaking it, saying, this is my body which is given for you, Acts 2:46 has the church breaking bread from house to house with gladness, and 1 Corinthians 10:16 asks, the bread which we break, is it not the communion of the body of Christ?
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the broken bread is the gospel in the hands: Jesus broke it for the hungry, broke it for His disciples the night He died, and the church has been breaking it ever since. I hold that nothing is lost in the breaking, because the hands that break the bread are the hands that feed the five thousand.
